images.caption: Figure 1:VAE Rhythm.(a) A4×4\timescausal VAE decodes frames in groups, illustrated on Sora frames. (b) As the VAE window shifts, its groups realign with those of the clip every four starts. The residualr⁡(k)r(k)of a typical Sora clip therefore oscillates, while that of a typical real clip stays nearly flat.
Figure 4:Barcode view.Residual profiles of up to 100 clips per group with one clip per row. Red is high and blue is low.

Figure 5:Overview.(a) A frozen video VAE has two uses. The periodicity of its phase scan gives the zero-shot scorescs_{c}, and its round trip creates the VAE pairs, which differ only by VAE decoding. (b) On one frozen DINOv3 backbone, CaDet trains an artifact path with the pairs and a semantic path without them. (c) The plug-in adds positive rhythm evidence to the score of any detector without retraining it. All plots, tables and the difference map are measured.
